def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster the tie-break below realises (current contract cannot see swizzle): along the shorter grid side.
    # M<=N: identity (M-fastest), A panels are the fast-dim panels; M>N: horizontal (N-fastest), B panels are.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    # DRAM leg: ONE consistent byte count for that raster, plus C writes, split-K partials, and spills.
    # The SM roof uses the slower of the compute and L2-feed legs, while DRAM combines imperfectly with it.
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency the norm cannot see: register-staged 2-stage mainloop and CTA-wide barrier over more warps.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    # Split-K time model with an interior optimum, in log2 time.
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    # Pure tie-break among raster variants; shorter-side raster is preferred by the fixed sign.
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    # Multistage fill/drain is most exposed for short K loops; resource pressure makes
    # deeper pipelines especially costly when they cannot be hidden by residency.
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        if p.K < 1024:
            s = s + w[15] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
            s = s + w[16] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
            s = s + w[17] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[18] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        else:
            s = s + w[19] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
            s = s + w[20] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
            s = s + w[21] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[22] * f.shared_memory_pressure
    else:
        if p.K < 1024:
            s = s + w[23] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
            s = s + w[24] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
            s = s + w[25] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[26] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        else:
            s = s + w[27] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
            s = s + w[28] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
            s = s + w[29] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[30] * f.shared_memory_pressure
    # A narrower branch isolates rectangular grids with enough work to amortize launch noise,
    # but not enough output surface to make the ordinary populated-grid geometry adequate.
    if (p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.5 and
            p.output_work_per_sm < 1000000.0 and
            p.log_min_dim > 5):
        s = s + w[3] * (f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0)
        s = s + w[4] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
        s = s + w[5] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[6] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        # Boundary and dispatch inefficiency are jointly exposed in this partially amortized regime.
        s = s + w[31] * (np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste) / np.log2(301.0))
        s = s + w[32] * (np.log2(1.0 / (1.0 - np.clip(f.tail_waste, 0.0, 0.99))) / np.log2(100.0))
        s = s + w[33] * f.wave_count_deficit
        s = s + w[34] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
        s = s + w[35] * (f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0)
    elif p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.5:
        s = s + w[3] * (f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0)
        s = s + w[4] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
        s = s + w[5] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[6] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        s = s + w[7] * f.register_file_pressure
        s = s + w[8] * f.shared_memory_pressure
    else:
        s = s + w[9] * (f.tile_aspect_mismatch / 20.0)
        s = s + w[10] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
        s = s + w[11] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[12] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        s = s + w[13] * f.register_file_pressure
        s = s + w[14] * f.shared_memory_pressure
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster tie-break: use the shorter grid side's raster model.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Register staging and CTA-wide barrier effects are retained from the parent.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst

    # When each SM has abundant output work and the problem is large, tile
    # family choice is already covered by the absolute model above.  Use the
    # tile-local split excess and wave/tail state to choose split counts.
    if p.output_work_per_sm > 4096 and p.log_flops > 32:
        s = s + w[3] * f.splitk_excess_log
        s = s + w[4] * f.wave_count_deficit
        s = s + w[5] * f.tail_waste
    else:
        # With insufficient output work, retain the absolute split-K model so
        # that under-splitting and idle SMs remain explicitly priced.
        s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time

    # Memory/feed-limited shapes trade tile geometry against operand reuse and
    # per-CTA amortisation.  Rectangular outputs have a different useful
    # row/column geometry from square-like outputs.
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        if p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.5:
            s = s + w[6] * f.tile_aspect_mismatch
            s = s + w[7] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
            s = s + w[8] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
            s = s + w[9] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        else:
            s = s + w[10] * f.tile_aspect_mismatch
            s = s + w[11] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
            s = s + w[12] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
            s = s + w[13] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
    else:
        # Compute-bound shapes still benefit from amortised tile work, but
        # resource pressure is the stronger constraint on large tiles.
        s = s + w[14] * f.tile_aspect_mismatch
        s = s + w[15] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
        s = s + w[16] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[17] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        s = s + w[18] * f.register_file_pressure
        s = s + w[19] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        s = s + w[20] * f.occupancy_deficit
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster the tie-break below realises (current contract cannot see swizzle): along the shorter grid side.
    # M<=N: identity (M-fastest), A panels are the fast-dim panels; M>N: horizontal (N-fastest), B panels are.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    # DRAM leg and the slower of the SM compute and L2-feed paths.
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency corrections retained from the parent.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    # Existing split-K roofline model retained as the base split-count predictor.
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    # Reduction mode has different costs in the memory and compute regimes.  In the
    # memory regime, global partial traffic is the dominant parallel-reduction cost.
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1:
        s = s + w[3] * f.serial_reduction_dependency
        s = s + w[4] * f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction
        s = s + w[5] * np.abs(f.splitk_excess_log)
    else:
        # For saturated compute grids, tile-family efficiency and replicated operand
        # work become visible before the active norm's small-resource preference.
        if p.output_work_per_sm > 1024:
            s = s + w[6] * f.serial_reduction_dependency
            s = s + w[7] * f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction
            s = s + w[8] * f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction
            s = s + w[9] * np.abs(f.splitk_excess_log)
            s = s + w[10] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
            s = s + w[11] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
            s = s + w[12] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
            s = s + w[13] * f.resident_block_scarcity
            s = s + w[14] * f.wave_count_deficit
            s = s + w[15] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[16] * f.log_roofline_time_mraster
        else:
            # For compute-bound but sparsely populated grids, retain the parent's
            # reduction and active-resource ordering without saturated-grid terms.
            s = s + w[6] * f.serial_reduction_dependency
            s = s + w[7] * f.parallel_reduction_compute_fraction
            s = s + w[8] * f.parallel_reduction_traffic_fraction
            s = s + w[9] * np.abs(f.splitk_excess_log)
    # Small swizzle/raster interaction: code-size raster evidence matters more when
    # the selected width-1 raster is under greater panel/cache traffic pressure.
    s = s + w[17] * np.log2(1.0 + d) * (sgn * (f.tm_log_inst - 8.0) / 8.0)
    # Pure raster tie-break among variants differing only in instruction count.
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster tie-break: along the shorter output-grid side.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Existing efficiency corrections and interior split-K time model.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    # Tile geometry and thread-level amortization are distinct from boundary waste.
    s = s + w[3] * np.log2(1.0 + f.tile_aspect_mismatch)
    s = s + w[4] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
    # Bandwidth-bound shapes emphasize replicated operand traffic and tile intensity;
    # compute-bound shapes emphasize residency and resource limits instead.
    if p.roofline_ratio < 1.0:
        s = s + w[5] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[6] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        s = s + w[7] * f.resident_block_scarcity
        s = s + w[8] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        s = s + w[9] * f.register_file_pressure
        # Explicitly strengthen selected width-1 traffic; the other terms proxy
        # swizzle-dependent panel reuse and wave balance.
        s = s + w[14] * np.log2(1.0 + np.where(p.M > p.N, f.dram_w1_hz_ratio, f.dram_w1_id_ratio))
        s = s + w[15] * np.log2(f.operand_tile_traffic_ratio)
        s = s + w[16] * (-np.log2(np.maximum(1e-6, 1.0 - f.tail_waste)))
    else:
        s = s + w[10] * f.tile_roofline_deficit
        s = s + w[11] * f.resident_block_scarcity
        s = s + w[12] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        s = s + w[13] * f.register_file_pressure
        # Raster traffic remains useful outside the bandwidth regime, while
        # tail imbalance remains a distinct wave-level cost.
        s = s + w[17] * np.log2(1.0 + np.where(p.M > p.N, f.dram_w1_hz_ratio, f.dram_w1_id_ratio))
        s = s + w[18] * (-np.log2(np.maximum(1e-6, 1.0 - f.tail_waste)))
    return s
